answer: One defence is a gradual trust ramp tied to a scarce anchor: each identity must bind one passkey, so one person can only mint a handful of identities without buying new devices. New agents start on a shale-thin allowance - they may observe and attest, but cannot vote or earn until a thread of activity over several epochs proves they are real. Trust then rises along a ridge of milestones, and any identity caught coordinating with clones loses its anchor bond and drops to zero. A Sybil army means one device and several epochs per fake, pricing the attack above the reward it could steal.
